env.name: cmv
env.description:
Measure the supplied hypotheses; do not discover, rewrite or refine them. Each feature is
one scalar measurement of a discussion row, not a separate observation for every comment.
The full supplied corpus contains 2,000 rows: 1,000 changed and 1,000 unchanged outcomes.
Describe associations, not proven causal effects or prospective prediction.

Columns:
  - post_created_utc: Unix timestamp for the original post, not a comment or score-measurement
    timestamp. Response delay cannot be calculated from it.
  - title: the original poster's (OP's) heading or claim statement, not the argument body.
  - argument: the OP's explanation of their view. Use this field for argument-body measurements;
    include title only when the requested scope includes the heading or when it is needed to
    interpret a comment's target. Text can contain quotations, edits and outcome announcements.
  - OC_comments: a JSON-encoded list of available counter-argument comments by OTHER users,
    not the OP. Parse the list before counting comments, words or semantic instances.
    Specify any/all/count/share/mean explicitly. List order is not rank, importance or chronology.
    If properties must coexist in one comment, assess their conjunction within that comment;
    separate comments cannot jointly satisfy it. The row-level extractor still returns one scalar.
    List length counts comments, not necessarily distinct commenters. No per-comment outcomes,
    scores or timestamps are supplied. OP-language measurements use title/argument instead.
  - conversation: formatted interaction text overlapping OC_comments, not extra independent
    evidence. It may include later replies and explicit view-change announcements. Do not use
    it as an initial-argument snapshot. When interaction is required, specify speaker/turn
    selection. Disclose unknown reply timing and do not infer reply links from speaker order alone.
  - log_length: a supplied log-transformed length measure. Construction, source text, log base
    and timing are undocumented. When named by the hypothesis, use the supplied value and state
    that limitation; do not equate it with argument word count or reconstruct its log base.
  - post_score: the observed original-post score, not a comment score, voter count or initial
    endorsement. Its measurement time relative to the outcome is unknown; post_created_utc
    does not establish that timing.
  - delta: OUTCOME, 1 if the OP changed their view, else 0. Never a predictor or annotation input.
  - post_id, comment_id: identifiers, never predictors.

Attribution and unavailable measurements:
  - No measured personality scores, Big Five questionnaires or author demographics are supplied.
    A personality inference from writing is a linguistic proxy, not an observed trait; do not
    substitute it silently when the hypothesis requires an unavailable measurement.
  - Distinguish the author's own assertions or experiences from attributed quotations.
    An external source cited as support can count for an evidence feature without making the
    source's wording or experience the author's own. Background/rebuttal quotations are not
    automatically adopted support. Apply this distinction to OP text and other users' comments.
    Quotation marks alone do not establish another speaker.

Computation and source suitability:
  - Use code for raw counts, regex/literal matching, supplied numeric columns and fixed
    computational recipes. Use a prompt when the measurement requires understanding meaning.
    Do not add semantic filtering to a raw count or URL detector merely because outcome text
    may occur in its source. Disclose that contamination risk; raw text is not outcome-free.
  - Semantic feature specs must exclude OP view-change/delta-award announcements, post-outcome
    resolution updates and reports of the outcome as evidence of the construct. Generic
    platform/delta-rule discussion remains eligible. Explicitly requested semantic exclusions
    remain part of any measurement; never remove one just to force code.
  - Use current supplied text unless the hypothesis restricts time. Deleting edits does not
    recover initial/pre-outcome text. No supplied comment/edit timestamps establish timing.
    If a required temporal measurement is unavailable, explain it and set term=null.
  - delta remains the fixed outcome. A hypothesis requiring a different outcome or an
    outcome-revealing predictor is unsupported: preserve the claim, explain it and set
    term=null rather than substituting another test or a cleaned concession/attitude proxy.

decomposed.hypothesis: Discussions where the original argument includes explicit comparisons to established scientific or historical norms are associated with lower view change than those without such comparisons.

features.name: argument_compares_to_science_history_norms
features.definition: Does the OP's argument text explicitly compare the topic or claim to an established scientific or historical norm, standard, or precedent?
features.spec: Read only the `argument` column (OP's own body text). Return 1 if the OP's own assertions explicitly compare their subject or claim to an established scientific norm/consensus/standard or an established historical norm/precedent/standard (e.g., 'like in the scientific consensus on X', 'historically, societies treated Y as the norm, and this is similar/different'). Return 0 if no such explicit comparison is present. Generic mentions of science or history without a comparison to the claim do not count. Quoted material counts only if the OP adopts it as their own comparison. Ignore any OP view-change/delta-award announcements, post-outcome edits or updates, and reports of the outcome; do not treat them as evidence. Missing or malformed argument gives null; empty text gives 0.

decomposed.h0: Discussions whose argument has explicit comparisons to established scientific or historical norms (argument_compares_to_science_history_norms=1) have the same view-change (delta) rate as those without.
decomposed.h1: Discussions with argument_compares_to_science_history_norms=1 have lower view-change (delta) rate than those with 0.
decomposed.note: Association only. Operational assumption: 'established scientific or historical norms' is judged by the LLM from the OP's argument text alone; title excluded. Current argument text may contain edits or outcome announcements (contamination/timing risk); the prompt ignores them, but deleting edits cannot recover original text. Linear probability model on binary delta.

decomposed.hypothesis: Arguments expressing explicit fear of social rejection or isolation are associated with lower view-change rates than arguments stating beliefs without emotional self-defense.

features.name: explicit_fear_social_rejection
features.definition: Does the OP's argument explicitly express fear of social rejection or isolation (e.g., being shunned, ostracized, disliked or left alone for holding or voicing the view)?
features.spec: Read only the OP's argument text. Return 1 if the OP, in their own voice, explicitly states fear or worry of social rejection, ostracism, being judged/shunned, or isolation/loneliness as a consequence connected to the view. Return 0 otherwise. Fears attributed to others or merely quoted and not adopted by the OP do not count. Ignore any view-change/delta-award announcements, post-outcome edits or reports of the outcome; they are not evidence. Empty or missing argument gives null.

features.name: belief_without_emotional_self_defense
features.definition: Does the OP's argument state beliefs and reasoning without any emotional self-defense (no expressed fear, hurt, defensiveness or protective emotional appeal)?
features.spec: Read only the OP's argument text. Return 1 if the OP's own assertions state beliefs/reasons without any emotional self-defense, meaning no expressed fear, anxiety, hurt, defensive justification of self or pre-emptive protection against judgment. Return 0 if any such emotional self-defense is present (including fear of social rejection or isolation). Quoted material not adopted by the OP is ignored. Ignore OP view-change/delta announcements, post-outcome edits and reports of the outcome. Empty or missing argument gives null.

decomposed.h0: Rows with explicit_fear_social_rejection have the same or higher delta rate than rows with belief_without_emotional_self_defense.
decomposed.h1: Rows with explicit_fear_social_rejection have a lower delta rate than rows with belief_without_emotional_self_defense.
decomposed.note: Both comparison groups are measured. With both included, the fear coefficient is relative to the omitted group (other emotional self-defense without social-rejection fear), not directly versus plain belief statements; the contrast beta_fear - beta_plain is not a single design-matrix term, so the test is only approximate. Fear is expected to be rare. Argument text is current text and may contain post-outcome edits or delta announcements (contamination/timing risk); prompts exclude them. Association only, not causal.

decomposed.hypothesis: Counter-arguments that cite specific, functioning institutional precedents are associated with a higher probability of view change than those relying on abstract normative principles.

features.name: precedent_comment_share
features.definition: What proportion of counter-argument comments cite a specific, functioning institutional precedent (a real existing law, policy, court, organization or system that operates or has operated in practice) in support of their point?
features.spec: Parse OC_comments (JSON list of comments by other users). For each comment decide if the commenter themselves cites at least one specific, concrete institutional precedent as support: a named or clearly identifiable real law, policy, institution, country/state/city program or system that actually functions/functioned in practice (e.g. 'Portugal's decriminalization has reduced overdoses'). Hypothetical institutions, vague appeals ('some countries'), purely abstract principles, and anecdotes with no institution do not count. Quotations of others count only if the commenter adopts them as support. Use title/argument only to interpret the comment's target. Ignore any text announcing OP view change, delta awards, or outcome reports; these are not evidence. Output = number of qualifying comments / total comments, in [0,1]. Empty list -> null; malformed/missing -> null.

features.name: abstract_principle_comment_share
features.definition: What proportion of counter-argument comments rely on abstract normative principles (e.g. rights, fairness, morality, what ought to be) rather than specific institutional precedents?
features.spec: Parse OC_comments. For each comment decide if its main support is an abstract normative principle or value argument (e.g. fairness, liberty, justice, moral duty, 'people should') without citing a specific, functioning institutional precedent as its support. A comment that cites a specific functioning institutional precedent as its main support does not count; comments with neither (e.g. purely factual/personal/logical) do not count. Commenter's own assertions only; quotations count only if adopted. Use title/argument only to interpret the target. Ignore any OP view-change/delta announcements or outcome reports. Output = qualifying comments / total comments, in [0,1]. Empty list -> null; malformed/missing -> null.

decomposed.h0: Holding abstract_principle_comment_share fixed, precedent_comment_share has no association with the probability of view change.
decomposed.h1: Holding abstract_principle_comment_share fixed, higher precedent_comment_share is associated with a higher probability of view change.
decomposed.note: Both named groups are measured as separate shares. The OLS contrast (beta_precedent minus beta_abstract) is not directly expressible; the term tests only the precedent coefficient with abstract share controlled. Comment-level outcomes are unavailable, so this is a row-level association with delta. Groups can overlap or be neither. Comments are unordered, and current text may contain outcome announcements, which the prompts exclude. 'Functioning' is judged from the comment text only, with no external verification. Associations only, not causal.

decomposed.hypothesis: Discussions featuring longer precomputed log-transformed discussion length are associated with a higher likelihood of the original poster changing their view.

features.name: supplied_log_length
features.definition: What is the supplied precomputed log-transformed length value for the discussion?
features.spec: df['log_length'] cast to numeric with pd.to_numeric(errors='coerce'); missing or non-numeric gives null. Use the supplied value as is; do not recompute or change the log base.

decomposed.h0: Supplied log_length (supplied_log_length) has no association with the likelihood of the OP changing their view (delta).
decomposed.h1: Higher supplied_log_length is associated with a higher likelihood of the OP changing their view.
decomposed.note: The log_length construction, source text, log base and timing are undocumented, so it may not equal argument or conversation length and may include text post-dating or revealing the outcome. The supplied value is used as given. The test is a linear OLS association (a linear probability model on delta), not a causal effect.

decomposed.hypothesis: Discussions where the original argument contains explicit admissions of uncertainty are associated with a higher probability of view change than those asserting absolute certainty.

features.name: op_admits_uncertainty
features.definition: Does the original poster's argument text contain at least one explicit admission of the OP's own uncertainty about their view or claims?
features.spec: Read only `argument` (OP's own text). Return 1 if the OP's own assertions include at least one explicit admission of uncertainty about their own position or claims (e.g., 'I'm not sure', 'I could be wrong', 'I'm unsure whether', 'I might be mistaken'). Return 0 if none. Generic hedging words without an admission of the OP's uncertainty do not count. Do not count uncertainty in quoted text attributed to others unless the OP adopts it as their own. Ignore any OP view-change/delta-award announcements, edits reporting that the view changed, post-outcome updates, or reports of the outcome; these are not evidence. Return null if argument is missing or malformed; empty text gives 0.

features.name: op_asserts_absolute_certainty
features.definition: Does the original poster's argument text assert absolute certainty about their view, such as stating it is definitely true or cannot possibly be wrong?
features.spec: Read only `argument` (OP's own text). Return 1 if the OP's own assertions explicitly claim absolute certainty about their position (e.g., 'I am 100% certain', 'there is no possible way I'm wrong', 'this is undeniably/absolutely true', 'no doubt whatsoever'). Return 0 otherwise. Ordinary confident phrasing, or absolutes applied to side facts rather than certainty of the OP's view, do not count. Do not count quoted text attributed to others unless the OP adopts it. Ignore any OP view-change/delta-award announcements, post-outcome updates, or reports of the outcome. Return null if argument is missing or malformed; empty text gives 0.

decomposed.h0: Controlling for op_asserts_absolute_certainty, op_admits_uncertainty is not associated with the probability of view change.
decomposed.h1: Controlling for op_asserts_absolute_certainty, op_admits_uncertainty is associated with a higher probability of view change.
decomposed.note: Both comparison sides are measured separately; the claimed contrast (uncertainty minus certainty) is not a single coefficient in this OLS, so term tests only the uncertainty coefficient with certainty held fixed. The two features can overlap or both be 0 (neither group). Analysis is an association on a linear probability model, not causal. Argument text is current text and may contain edits or outcome announcements; semantic specs exclude these, but timing relative to the outcome is unknown.

decomposed.hypothesis: Counter-arguments frequently challenging multiple distinct factual premises within the argument are positively associated with view change.

features.name: share_comments_challenging_multiple_factual_premises
features.definition: What proportion of the counter-argument comments each challenge two or more distinct factual premises of the OP's argument?
features.spec: Parse OC_comments (JSON list of comments by users other than OP). Read title and argument only to identify the OP's factual (empirical, non-evaluative) premises and the target of each comment. For each comment, decide whether the commenter's own assertions challenge (dispute, rebut, or present contrary evidence against) at least two distinct factual premises of the OP's argument; challenges to values, logic only, or the same premise restated do not count as separate. Quoted material counts only if the commenter adopts it. Ignore any OP view-change/delta-award announcements, post-outcome resolution text, and reports of the outcome; they are not evidence. Output = (number of comments meeting the criterion) / (total number of comments), range 0-1. Empty list gives null; missing or malformed OC_comments gives null.

decomposed.h0: share_comments_challenging_multiple_factual_premises has no association with delta.
decomposed.h1: Higher share_comments_challenging_multiple_factual_premises is positively associated with delta.
decomposed.note: Operationalization: "frequently" is measured as the share of comments that each challenge at least two distinct factual premises (threshold of two taken from "multiple"). Factual vs. evaluative premises is a judgment call. Comment order, timing, and reply links are unknown. Comments may include text revealing outcomes; the prompt excludes these. Association only, not causal.

decomposed.hypothesis: Discussions where the original argument contains fewer counter-argument responses are associated with a lower likelihood of the original poster changing their view.

features.name: oc_comment_count
features.definition: How many counter-argument comments by other users are in the discussion's comment list?
features.spec: import json; lst=json.loads(df['OC_comments']); return len(lst) if isinstance(lst,list) else None. Empty list gives 0; missing or malformed JSON gives null. Counts list entries (comments), not distinct commenters.

decomposed.h0: oc_comment_count has no association with the likelihood that the OP changed their view (delta).
decomposed.h1: Higher oc_comment_count is associated with a higher likelihood of delta, so fewer counter-argument comments go with a lower likelihood.
decomposed.note: "Fewer counter-argument responses" is read as a lower count of comments in OC_comments, tested linearly. The text says "the original argument contains" these responses; I treated that as the discussion's comment list. Only the available comments are counted, so the list may be incomplete or selected, and the comment list may include comments that led to or followed the view change. Raw counting does not filter outcome announcements. Reply timing is unknown. The result is an association only, not causal. The outcome is delta, which is not used as a feature input.

decomposed.hypothesis: Discussions with at least three distinct counter-arguments in the posted comments are associated with a higher likelihood of the original poster changing their view.

features.name: distinct_counterargument_count
features.definition: How many distinct counter-arguments against the OP's view are made across the posted counter-argument comments?
features.spec: Parse OC_comments (JSON list of comments by users other than the OP). Use title and argument only to interpret what the OP's view is. Count the number of distinct counter-arguments (separate lines of reasoning, evidence or objections challenging the OP's view) across all comments. Multiple comments making the same point count once; one comment making several different points counts each. Count only the commenters' own assertions, not quotations of the OP or others unless adopted. Do not count content that is an OP view-change/delta-award announcement, post-outcome resolution update, or report of the outcome; generic platform/delta-rule discussion is not a counter-argument by itself. Output a non-negative integer. Empty list gives 0; missing or malformed OC_comments gives null.

features.name: has_three_or_more_distinct_counterarguments
features.definition: Does the discussion contain at least three distinct counter-arguments in the posted comments?
features.spec: df['has_three_or_more_distinct_counterarguments'] = (df['distinct_counterargument_count'] >= 3).astype(float).where(df['distinct_counterargument_count'].notna()). Null if `distinct_counterargument_count` is null.

decomposed.h0: Discussions with at least three distinct counter-arguments (has_three_or_more_distinct_counterarguments=1) have the same likelihood of OP view change as those with fewer.
decomposed.h1: Discussions with has_three_or_more_distinct_counterarguments=1 have a higher likelihood of OP view change than those with fewer than three.
decomposed.note: Association only, not causal. Distinctness of counter-arguments is judged semantically by an LLM; no scale beyond count is invented, and the threshold of 3 comes from the hypothesis. OC_comments are only the available comments, with unknown timing/order; they may include later replies or outcome-related text, which the prompt excludes, but source contamination risk remains. The outcome is binary and OLS gives a linear probability model.

decomposed.hypothesis: Discussions where the original post title uses absolute certainty markers are associated with a lower likelihood of the original poster changing their view.

features.name: title_absolute_certainty_marker
features.definition: Does the original post title use at least one absolute certainty marker (e.g., 'always', 'never', 'all', 'every', 'obviously', 'definitely')?
features.spec: Read only the title. Return 1 if the title itself, in the OP's own wording, contains at least one marker expressing absolute certainty or universality, such as always, never, all, every, everyone, no one, nobody, none, obviously, undeniably, definitely, certainly, absolutely, without a doubt, 100%, completely, or clearly asserting something is a fact beyond question. Words must function as absolute/certainty markers in context (e.g., 'all' in 'all-in-one' or 'never' inside a quoted title of a work does not count). Return 0 if none are present. Missing or empty title gives null. Ignore any OP view-change or delta-award announcements or outcome reports if they appear in the title; they are not evidence of the construct.

decomposed.h0: Title_absolute_certainty_marker has no association with the likelihood that the OP changed their view (delta).
decomposed.h1: Discussions with title_absolute_certainty_marker = 1 have a lower likelihood of delta than those with 0.
decomposed.note: Operational assumption: absolute certainty markers are judged by an LLM using a listed, non-exhaustive set of absolutes/universals in the title. Association only, not causal. Titles are current text and could in principle contain edit or outcome text, though this is unlikely. The OLS is a linear probability model.

decomposed.hypothesis: Discussions where original posts explicitly invite critique or use tentative language are associated with higher view-change rates than those using absolute, definitive declarations.

features.name: op_invites_critique_or_tentative
features.definition: Does the original post explicitly invite critique or counterarguments, or frame its own claims with tentative/hedged language?
features.spec: Read title and argument (OP's own text). Return 1 if the OP's own assertions explicitly invite critique/counterarguments/being challenged (e.g., 'point out where I'm wrong', 'convince me') or frame the main view with tentative language (e.g., 'I think', 'maybe', 'seems', 'to my knowledge', 'I'm not sure'). Return 0 if neither appears. Generic CMV boilerplate in the title prefix 'CMV:' alone does not count. Ignore quoted text from others unless OP adopts it. Ignore any OP view-change/delta-award announcements, post-outcome edits or reports of the outcome. Return null if both fields are missing/empty.

features.name: op_uses_absolute_declarations
features.definition: Does the original post state its main view using absolute, definitive declarations (e.g., all, never, always, certainly) without hedging?
features.spec: Read title and argument (OP's own text). Return 1 if the OP's main claim(s) are framed as absolute or definitive declarations (universal quantifiers such as all/every/never/always/no one, or certainty claims such as 'obviously', 'undeniably', 'it is a fact') in the OP's own voice. Return 0 otherwise. A post can score 1 on this and on `op_invites_critique_or_tentative` if both appear. Ignore quotations from others unless adopted. Ignore OP view-change/delta-award announcements, post-outcome edits or reports of the outcome. Return null if both fields are missing/empty.

decomposed.h0: Holding op_uses_absolute_declarations constant, op_invites_critique_or_tentative has no association with delta (view-change rate).
decomposed.h1: Holding op_uses_absolute_declarations constant, posts with op_invites_critique_or_tentative=1 have higher view-change rates.
decomposed.note: Both named groups are measured separately; overlap and neither-group cases are preserved. The contrast (tentative minus absolute) is not directly expressible as a single coefficient; the tested term is the tentative/invite coefficient with the absolute feature as covariate, and the absolute coefficient should be expected to be negative. Linear probability OLS; associations only. Text is current supplied text; edits/outcome announcements may be present and no timestamps establish timing, so contamination risk remains (specs exclude such announcements). Combining 'invites critique' with 'tentative language' as an OR follows the hypothesis wording.

decomposed.hypothesis: Discussions featuring counter-arguments that explicitly cite specific real-world examples are associated with higher likelihood of original view change.

features.name: counter_comment_cites_specific_example
features.definition: Does at least one counter-argument comment by another user explicitly cite a specific real-world example (named or concretely identifiable real event, case, person, place, study or instance) in support of its point?
features.spec: Parse OC_comments (JSON list of comments by users other than the OP). Return 1 if at least one comment, in its own words, explicitly cites a specific real-world example (concretely identifiable real event, case, person, organization, place, study, historical episode or documented instance), including an external source cited as support. Return 0 if no comment does (only generic claims, hypotheticals, or vague 'for example people...' without a specific real instance); return 0 for a valid empty list; null if OC_comments is missing or malformed. Use title/argument only to interpret a comment's target. Do not count mere quotations of the OP or background/rebuttal quotes that the commenter does not adopt as support. Exclude as evidence any OP view-change/delta-award announcements, post-outcome resolution updates or reports of the outcome (e.g., delta award messages). Hypothetical examples and the OP's own examples do not count. Do not use the conversation column or delta.

decomposed.h0: counter_comment_cites_specific_example has no association with the likelihood of OP view change (delta).
decomposed.h1: Discussions where at least one counter-argument comment cites a specific real-world example (counter_comment_cites_specific_example=1) have higher likelihood of OP view change.
decomposed.note: Operationalized "discussions featuring counter-arguments that cite specific real-world examples" as any available counter-comment doing so (not share or count). Comments are unordered, with no timing; association only, not causal. OC_comments may contain outcome announcements, which the prompt excludes as evidence. Comments available may be limited/selected, which could relate to the outcome.

decomposed.hypothesis: Counterarguments containing measured, logical reasoning are positively associated with the original poster changing their mind compared to those containing emotional aggression in ChangeMyView discussions.

features.name: share_logical_reasoning_comments
features.definition: What proportion of the counter-argument comments contain measured, logical reasoning (calm, structured argument from premises or evidence toward a conclusion)?
features.spec: Parse OC_comments (JSON list of comments by other users). For each comment decide whether it contains measured, logical reasoning: a calm, civil, structured argument (premises, evidence, or inference toward a conclusion) addressing the OP's view (use title/argument only for interpreting the target). A comment can count for this and also for emotional aggression; do not force exclusivity. Judge the comment author's own assertions, not text they merely quote from others unless adopted. Ignore any OP view-change/delta-award announcements, post-outcome resolution updates or reports of the outcome as evidence. Output = number of qualifying comments / total comments, in [0,1]. Empty list -> null; malformed/missing -> null.

features.name: share_emotionally_aggressive_comments
features.definition: What proportion of the counter-argument comments contain emotional aggression (hostile, insulting, angry or contemptuous language toward the OP or their view)?
features.spec: Parse OC_comments (JSON list of comments by other users). For each comment decide whether it contains emotional aggression in the commenter's own voice: hostile, insulting, angry, sneering or contemptuous language directed at the OP or their view/person. Mere disagreement or blunt but civil criticism does not count. Quoted text from others does not count unless adopted. Use title/argument only to interpret the target. Ignore any OP view-change/delta-award announcements, post-outcome updates or reports of the outcome. Output = number of aggressive comments / total comments, in [0,1]. Empty list -> null; malformed/missing -> null.

decomposed.h0: Holding share_emotionally_aggressive_comments fixed, share_logical_reasoning_comments has no association with delta (coefficient = 0).
decomposed.h1: Holding share_emotionally_aggressive_comments fixed, higher share_logical_reasoning_comments is associated with higher probability of delta (coefficient > 0).
decomposed.note: Both named sides are measured; the contract cannot test the contrast beta_logical - beta_aggressive directly, so the term tests the logical share's coefficient while controlling for aggression share (the aggression coefficient is also informative). Comparison is at row level (shares of comments), not per comment. The two categories are not mutually exclusive. OC_comments may contain later replies and outcome announcements; the prompts exclude those as evidence, but the timing of comments is unknown. Associations only, not causal effects.

decomposed.hypothesis: Discussions where counter-arguments explicitly quote and refute specific factual claims in the original post are associated with higher rates of view change.

features.name: any_comment_quotes_and_refutes_op_factual_claim
features.definition: Does at least one counter-argument comment explicitly quote a specific factual claim from the original post and refute that claim in the same comment?
features.spec: Parse OC_comments (JSON list of comments by users other than OP). Use title and argument only to identify the OP's factual claims. Output 1 if at least one single comment both (a) explicitly quotes (verbatim or clearly marked near-verbatim, e.g. blockquote/'>' or quotation marks) a specific factual claim stated in the OP's title/argument, and (b) argues in that same comment that this claim is factually wrong or unsupported. Both conditions must be met within the same comment; separate comments cannot combine. Quoting only opinions/values, quoting without refuting, or refuting without quoting gives no credit. Ignore any text that is an OP view-change/delta-award announcement, post-outcome resolution update or report of the outcome; such text is not evidence. Output 0 if no comment qualifies, 0 for a valid empty list, null if OC_comments is missing or malformed.

decomposed.h0: any_comment_quotes_and_refutes_op_factual_claim has no association with the probability of view change (delta).
decomposed.h1: Rows with any_comment_quotes_and_refutes_op_factual_claim = 1 have a higher rate of view change than rows with 0.
decomposed.note: Operationalized "discussions where counter-arguments quote and refute" as at least one comment doing both. OLS on binary outcome (linear probability model). Association only. OC_comments may contain later content or outcome announcements, and timing/order is unknown; these are excluded from the semantic judgment but the text itself is not outcome-free. Factual vs. opinion claim distinction is judged by the annotator.

decomposed.hypothesis: Discussions where counter-arguments explicitly validate the original poster's personal dignity or effort before introducing corrective logic are associated with higher view-change rates than purely logical refutations.

features.name: validates_dignity_before_correction
features.definition: Does at least one counter-argument comment explicitly validate the OP's personal dignity or effort before introducing corrective logic in that same comment?
features.spec: Parse OC_comments (JSON list of comments by other users). Return 1 if at least one single comment first explicitly validates the OP's personal dignity, worth, or effort (e.g., praising their effort, respecting them as a person, acknowledging their sincere attempt) and afterwards, in the same comment, introduces corrective logic or a counter-argument aimed at the OP's view. Validation must be directed at the OP personally, not merely agreeing with a point or generic politeness. Order within the comment matters: validation must precede the correction. Separate comments cannot jointly satisfy it. Use title and argument only to interpret the comment's target. Ignore quoted text unless the commenter adopts it. Do not count OP view-change/delta-award announcements, thanks after the view changed, or reports of the outcome as evidence. Generic delta-rule discussion is eligible but not itself validation. Return 0 if the list is valid but empty or no comment qualifies; null if OC_comments is missing or malformed.

features.name: purely_logical_refutation_only
features.definition: Are the counter-argument comments purely logical refutations, with no comment explicitly validating the OP's personal dignity or effort?
features.spec: Parse OC_comments. Return 1 if there is at least one comment, at least one comment offers logical refutation or corrective reasoning against the OP's view, and no comment explicitly validates the OP's personal dignity or effort (praise of effort, respect for the OP as a person) at any position. Return 0 if any comment contains such validation, or if no comment offers logical refutation. Return null if OC_comments is missing or malformed or the list is empty. Use title and argument only to interpret targets. Ignore quoted text unless adopted. Exclude OP view-change/delta-award announcements, post-outcome updates and reports of the outcome as evidence.

decomposed.h0: Discussions with validates_dignity_before_correction equal to 1 have the same view-change rate as discussions with purely_logical_refutation_only equal to 1 (coefficient on validates_dignity_before_correction is 0).
decomposed.h1: Discussions with validates_dignity_before_correction equal to 1 have a higher view-change rate than purely logical refutation discussions (coefficient on validates_dignity_before_correction is greater than 0).
decomposed.note: The contract cannot express the contrast beta_validate - beta_pure directly; the term tests only the validation coefficient with the pure-logic indicator as a covariate, so it is not an exact A-vs-B contrast. The two features are constructed to be mutually exclusive (validation anywhere gives pure=0), leaving a baseline of discussions with neither feature. Comment order is unknown across comments; the within-comment order is judged from text. Source text may contain outcome announcements or later replies; these are excluded in the semantic specs, but risk of residual contamination remains. Associations only.

decomposed.hypothesis: Discussions featuring counter-arguments that provide concrete real-world examples are associated with a higher likelihood of view change than those relying primarily on abstract reasoning.

features.name: share_comments_concrete_examples
features.definition: What proportion of the counter-argument comments provide at least one concrete real-world example (specific case, event, person, data instance or lived situation) in support of their point?
features.spec: Parse OC_comments (JSON list of comments by users other than the OP). Use title and argument only to interpret what each comment targets. For each comment, decide whether the commenter's own text offers at least one concrete real-world example (a specific named or described real case, event, person, situation, statistic instance or personal experience) used to support the counter-argument. Hypothetical/generic scenarios without a real-world anchor do not count. Quoted text from others counts only if the commenter adopts it as their example. Ignore any OP view-change/delta-award announcements, post-outcome updates or reports of the outcome as evidence. Output = number of qualifying comments / total comments, in [0,1]. Empty list -> null; missing or malformed -> null.

features.name: share_comments_primarily_abstract
features.definition: What proportion of the counter-argument comments rely primarily on abstract reasoning (general principles, logic, definitions, hypotheticals) rather than concrete real-world examples?
features.spec: Parse OC_comments (JSON list of comments by users other than the OP). Use title and argument only to interpret each comment's target. For each comment, decide whether its main support is abstract reasoning (general principles, logical argument, definitions, conceptual distinctions, hypotheticals) with no concrete real-world example carrying the argument. Comments that primarily rest on a concrete real-world example do not count. Quoted text from others counts as the commenter's reasoning only if adopted. Ignore any OP view-change/delta-award announcements, post-outcome updates or reports of the outcome as evidence. Output = number of such comments / total comments, in [0,1]. Empty list -> null; missing or malformed -> null.

decomposed.h0: share_comments_concrete_examples has no association with delta likelihood, holding share_comments_primarily_abstract fixed.
decomposed.h1: Higher share_comments_concrete_examples is associated with higher likelihood of view change, holding share_comments_primarily_abstract fixed.
decomposed.note: Hypothesis is a comparison of concrete-example vs primarily-abstract discussions; both sides are measured, but the contract cannot test the contrast beta_example - beta_abstract directly; the term tests only the example share conditional on the abstract share. Shares need not sum to 1 (a comment may have both or neither); comment order, chronology and per-comment outcomes are unavailable. OLS on a binary outcome (linear probability). Comment text may contain outcome announcements (semantic prompts exclude them), and the conversation column is not used. Associations only, not causal.

decomposed.hypothesis: Discussions where counter-arguments explicitly engage with the specific examples or premises cited in the original argument text are associated with a higher likelihood of view change.

features.name: cc_engages_op_examples_premises
features.definition: Does at least one counter-argument comment explicitly engage with a specific example or premise cited in the OP's argument text?
features.spec: Parse OC_comments (JSON list of other users' comments). Read title and argument for context to identify the specific examples, cases, evidence or premises the OP cites. Return 1 if at least one comment explicitly addresses (e.g., rebuts, questions, accepts, or analyzes) a specific example or premise stated in the OP's text, by referring to its particular content rather than only the general conclusion or generic points. Return 0 if comments exist but none do so. Empty or no comments: 0; malformed/missing input: null. Ignore OP view-change/delta-award announcements, post-outcome updates, and reports of the outcome as evidence of engagement. Text quoted from the OP counts only as a target being engaged with; the comment must actually respond to it. List order carries no meaning.

decomposed.h0: cc_engages_op_examples_premises has no association with the likelihood of view change (delta).
decomposed.h1: Higher cc_engages_op_examples_premises is associated with a higher likelihood of view change (delta).
decomposed.note: Hypothesis operationalized as any-comment engagement (binary), since "discussions where counter-arguments engage" is not quantified. Association only, not causal. Comment order/timing unknown; current text may contain outcome announcements, which the prompt is told to ignore. Linear probability OLS on delta.

decomposed.hypothesis: Discussions featuring counter-arguments that introduce concrete, personal labor-process details are associated with higher view-change rates than those relying solely on abstract normative principles.

features.name: has_personal_labor_detail_comment
features.definition: Does at least one counter-argument comment introduce concrete, personal details of how work or labor is actually done (e.g. the commenter's own or first-hand job tasks, workflow, hours, or conditions)?
features.spec: Parse OC_comments (JSON list of other users' comments); use title and argument only to interpret the target. Return 1 if at least one comment, in the commenter's own assertions (not quotations of others unless adopted), gives concrete, personal, first-hand details of a labor process (specific job tasks, workflow, schedules, tools, working conditions, hands-on experience of doing work). Return 0 if none does. Empty list gives 0; missing or malformed gives null. Ignore OP view-change or delta-award announcements, post-outcome updates and reports of the outcome as evidence. Generic abstract statements about work do not count; the text is current and comment timing is unknown.

features.name: only_abstract_normative_counterarguments
features.definition: Do the counter-argument comments rely solely on abstract normative principles, with no concrete personal labor-process details in any comment?
features.spec: Parse OC_comments; use title and argument only for context. Return 1 if the list is nonempty, at least one comment argues from abstract normative principles (e.g. rights, fairness, ethics, what ought to be), and no comment introduces concrete personal details of a labor process (specific job tasks, workflow, conditions, hands-on work experience) in the commenter's own assertions. Return 0 otherwise (including when any such labor detail exists or when comments are neither normative nor labor-detailed). Empty list gives 0; missing or malformed gives null. Ignore OP view-change or delta-award announcements, post-outcome updates and reports of the outcome as evidence. Quotations count only if adopted by the commenter.

decomposed.h0: Holding `only_abstract_normative_counterarguments` fixed, has_personal_labor_detail_comment is not associated with delta (view-change) rate.
decomposed.h1: Discussions with has_personal_labor_detail_comment=1 have a higher view-change rate than those with only_abstract_normative_counterarguments=1 (reference: neither).
decomposed.note: The claimed contrast is beta_labor minus beta_abstract; the coefficient on has_personal_labor_detail_comment is relative to the neither-group reference, not to the abstract-only group, so it only approximates the claim. The contrast would need a linear-combination test. Operational assumptions: "personal" means first-hand or commenter-specific; "solely abstract" means no labor detail in any comment. Source risks: OC_comments and conversation text may include later replies or outcome announcements; the prompts exclude them, but comment timing is unknown. The association is not causal.

decomposed.hypothesis: Discussions where counter-arguments explicitly quantify systemic material harms to third parties rather than asserting propositional falsity are associated with a higher likelihood of view change.

features.name: any_quantified_systemic_harm_comment
features.definition: Does at least one counter-argument comment explicitly quantify systemic material harms to third parties (e.g., with numbers, amounts, rates or counts of people affected)?
features.spec: Parse OC_comments (JSON list of comments by other users). Use title and argument only to interpret what a comment targets. Return 1 if at least one comment, in the commenter's own assertion (not an unadopted quotation), explicitly quantifies material harms (e.g., deaths, money lost, jobs, health, poverty, displacement) that fall on third parties (people other than the OP and commenter) at a systemic/societal scale, giving specific numbers, magnitudes, rates or counts. Vague claims of harm without quantification, purely personal anecdotes, and purely abstract/logical objections return 0 for that comment. Return 0 if no comment qualifies, 0 for a valid empty list, null if OC_comments is missing or malformed. Ignore any text announcing that the OP changed their view, delta awards, or post-outcome updates; these are not evidence.

features.name: any_propositional_falsity_comment
features.definition: Does at least one counter-argument comment assert that a claim made by the OP is factually or logically false, without relying on quantified harms to third parties?
features.spec: Parse OC_comments. Use title and argument to identify OP claims. Return 1 if at least one comment, in the commenter's own assertion (not an unadopted quotation), asserts that a proposition/claim of the OP is false, incorrect or unsupported (factual or logical refutation) rather than arguing from quantified material harm to third parties. Return 0 if none do, 0 for a valid empty list, null if OC_comments is missing or malformed. Ignore OP view-change/delta announcements, post-outcome updates and reports of the outcome as evidence.

decomposed.h0: any_quantified_systemic_harm_comment has no association with delta, holding any_propositional_falsity_comment constant.
decomposed.h1: any_quantified_systemic_harm_comment is positively associated with delta (higher view-change likelihood), holding any_propositional_falsity_comment constant.
decomposed.note: The hypothesis is a contrast (harm-quantifying vs falsity-asserting counter-arguments); the OLS term tests harm-quantification conditional on falsity-assertion, not an exact difference of coefficients. Both are any-comment, row-level measures; a discussion may have both or neither. Comments are unordered with no timestamps; OC_comments may include text after the outcome (view-change announcements), so contamination risk remains despite semantic exclusions. Association only, not causal.

decomposed.hypothesis: Discussions where counter-arguments identify logical contradictions within the original post's own stated premises are associated with higher view-change rates than those citing external evidence.

features.name: any_comment_identifies_internal_contradiction
features.definition: Does at least one counter-argument comment identify a logical contradiction within the original post's own stated premises?
features.spec: Parse OC_comments (JSON list of other users' comments). Use title and argument only to interpret the OP's stated premises. Return 1 if at least one comment, in its own assertion, argues that the OP's stated premises are mutually inconsistent or self-contradictory (e.g. premise A conflicts with premise B or with the OP's conclusion by the OP's own logic). Return 0 if none do. Disagreement from outside facts, or general logical criticism not showing contradiction among the OP's own premises, does not count. Ignore quoted text unless the commenter adopts it. Ignore OP view-change/delta-award announcements, post-outcome updates and reports of the outcome as evidence. Empty list gives 0; missing/malformed OC_comments gives null.

features.name: any_comment_cites_external_evidence
features.definition: Does at least one counter-argument comment cite external evidence (e.g. data, studies, sources, or documented facts) against the original post's view?
features.spec: Parse OC_comments. Return 1 if at least one comment itself cites external evidence such as statistics, studies, named sources, links, historical records or documented examples to counter the OP's view. An external source cited as support counts, without being the commenter's own experience. Mere opinion, personal reasoning without outside evidence, or quoted OP text does not count. Ignore OP view-change/delta-award announcements, post-outcome updates and reports of outcome as evidence. Empty list gives 0; missing/malformed gives null.

features.name: contradiction_minus_external_evidence
features.definition: Difference between presence of internal-contradiction counter-arguments and presence of external-evidence counter-arguments in a discussion.
features.spec: df['any_comment_identifies_internal_contradiction'] - df['any_comment_cites_external_evidence']; null if either is null. Values: 1 (contradiction only), 0 (both or neither), -1 (evidence only).

decomposed.h0: There is no association between contradiction_minus_external_evidence and delta (view-change) rate.
decomposed.h1: Higher contradiction_minus_external_evidence (internal-contradiction counter-arguments without external-evidence ones) is associated with a higher view-change rate.
decomposed.note: Operationalized the comparison as a difference of two any-presence indicators, so discussions with both or neither score 0; this is a linear-probability contrast and the two components are not tested separately. 'Citing external evidence' is taken as any comment citing outside evidence. Comments are unordered, with no timestamps; OC_comments may contain delta announcements or outcome text (excluded in the semantic specs). Association only, not causal. Overlap cases are retained as 0.

decomposed.hypothesis: Discussions where counter-arguments provide specific factual data or verifiable citations are associated with a higher likelihood of the original poster changing their view.

features.name: any_oc_specific_data_or_citation
features.definition: Does at least one counter-argument comment provide specific factual data or a verifiable citation in support of its point?
features.spec: Parse OC_comments (JSON list of comments by users other than the OP). Return 1 if at least one comment itself offers specific factual data (concrete statistics, figures, dates, named studies or documented facts) or a verifiable citation (named source, link, publication, law or case that could be looked up) as support for its argument. A source cited as support counts even though its wording is not the commenter's own. Vague appeals, generic claims, opinions, anecdotes without checkable specifics, and quotations that are only background or are being rebutted do not count. Ignore any text announcing that the OP changed their view, delta awards, or post-outcome resolution updates; these are not evidence. Generic delta-rule discussion is not evidence either. Return 0 if the list is valid but empty or no comment qualifies; null if missing or malformed.

decomposed.h0: any_oc_specific_data_or_citation has no association with the likelihood of delta (OP view change).
decomposed.h1: Discussions with any_oc_specific_data_or_citation = 1 have higher likelihood of OP view change than those with 0.
decomposed.note: Operationalized "counter-arguments provide specific data or citations" as at least one comment doing so (any), since no threshold was specified. Comments are unordered and untimed; OC_comments may include text after the outcome, and the extractor is instructed to ignore view-change announcements. Association only, not causal.

decomposed.hypothesis: Discussions where the original argument contains explicit polite apology phrases are associated with a lower likelihood of view change compared to arguments without such phrases.

features.name: argument_has_polite_apology_phrase
features.definition: Does the original argument text contain an explicit polite apology phrase (e.g., 'sorry', 'I apologize', 'my apologies', 'pardon me', 'excuse me')?
features.spec: Read df['argument'] only. If missing or not a string, return null. Else case-insensitive regex search with word boundaries for: \b(sorry|apologi[sz]e[sd]?|apologizing|apologising|apology|apologies|my bad|pardon( me)?|excuse me|forgive me)\b. Return 1 if any match, else 0 (empty string gives 0). Raw literal matching over current text; quotations are not distinguished from the OP's own words, and the text may include edits or post-outcome announcements (contamination/timing risk not filtered). Title, comments and conversation are not read.

decomposed.h0: argument_has_polite_apology_phrase has no association with the likelihood of view change (delta).
decomposed.h1: Arguments with argument_has_polite_apology_phrase = 1 are associated with a lower likelihood of view change than arguments without.
decomposed.note: Operational assumption: 'explicit polite apology phrases' is operationalized as a fixed keyword list (sorry, apologize, my apologies, pardon, excuse me, forgive me, etc.); the list is an assumption and may include non-apology uses (e.g., 'sorry to say'). Mechanical match does not separate quotations from the OP's own words. The argument text is current text and may contain edits or delta/view-change announcements; timing is unknown. Association only, not causal.

decomposed.hypothesis: Original posts featuring first-person vulnerable admissions are associated with higher view-change likelihood than those containing distant, third-person observations.

features.name: op_first_person_vulnerable_admission
features.definition: Does the OP's own text contain a first-person vulnerable admission (the OP admitting a personal struggle, fear, uncertainty, mistake, shame or weakness about themselves)?
features.spec: Read title and argument (OP's own words). Return 1 if the OP, in their own first-person assertions, admits something personally vulnerable (e.g. a struggle, fear, insecurity, mistake, shame, doubt or weakness about themselves). Return 0 if none. Ignore quoted text from others unless the OP adopts it as their own experience. Ignore view-change/delta announcements, post-outcome edits or updates, and reports of the outcome; they are not evidence. Generic discussion of delta/platform rules is eligible but is not itself a vulnerable admission. Null if both title and argument are missing/empty.

features.name: op_distant_third_person_observation
features.definition: Does the OP's own text contain distant, third-person observations (describing other people, groups or things from a detached standpoint rather than personal experience)?
features.spec: Read title and argument (OP's own words). Return 1 if the OP makes detached third-person observations about other people, groups, institutions or the world (without personal involvement). Return 0 if none. Ignore quoted text from others unless OP adopts it. Ignore view-change/delta announcements, post-outcome edits or updates, and outcome reports. Null if both title and argument are missing/empty.

decomposed.h0: Controlling for op_distant_third_person_observation, op_first_person_vulnerable_admission has no association with view change (delta).
decomposed.h1: Posts with op_first_person_vulnerable_admission=1 have higher view-change likelihood than those without, controlling for op_distant_third_person_observation.
decomposed.note: Both comparison groups are measured separately; the contract cannot test the direct contrast (beta_vulnerable − beta_distant), so the term tests the vulnerable-admission coefficient with the distant-observation covariate. Groups can overlap or both be absent. Uses current OP text, which may contain edits or outcome announcements; these are excluded from the semantic judgments but timing is unknown. Associations only, not causal.

decomposed.hypothesis: Discussions where counter-arguments include direct URLs or external links are associated with a higher likelihood of view change than those solely using internal text.

features.name: any_oc_comment_has_url
features.definition: Does at least one counter-argument comment contain a direct URL or external link?
features.spec: Parse OC_comments as a JSON list of strings; if missing/malformed return null. Empty list -> 0. Return 1 if any comment matches regex r'(https?://|www\.)[^\s)\]]+' (case-insensitive), else 0. Raw text match, no semantic filtering; markdown links [text](http...) are caught by the http match.

decomposed.h0: any_oc_comment_has_url has no association with the likelihood of view change (delta).
decomposed.h1: Discussions with any_oc_comment_has_url = 1 have a higher likelihood of view change than those without.
decomposed.note: Operational assumption: "solely internal text" is operationalized as no URL in any available counter-comment. Detection is literal; links without http/www (bare domains) are missed. Comments may include text written after or in response to the outcome, and timing is unknown; raw text is not outcome-free. Association only, via OLS (linear probability model).

decomposed.hypothesis: Discussions where counter-arguments employ specific, verifiable procedural examples are associated with higher original post view-change rates than those relying solely on abstract theoretical rebuttals.

features.name: any_procedural_example
features.definition: Does at least one counter-argument comment employ a specific, verifiable procedural example (a concrete named or checkable process, rule, case, or step-by-step instance) in its rebuttal?
features.spec: Parse OC_comments (JSON list of comments by users other than OP). Title and argument are context only for interpreting the comment target. Return 1 if at least one comment, in its own assertions, uses a specific, verifiable procedural example against the OP's view: a concrete, checkable instance of how a process, procedure, law, rule, system or case actually works or happened (e.g. named statute/procedure, documented case, specific step sequence, cited real-world instance). External sources cited as support count, without being treated as the commenter's own experience. Return 0 if comments exist but none does (rebuttals are abstract/theoretical, general principles, or hypotheticals without verifiable specifics). Quotations of the OP or others in background are not counted unless adopted by the commenter. Ignore any OP view-change/delta-award announcements, thanks, post-outcome updates or reports of the outcome as evidence. Empty or missing list: null (no comments to compare).

decomposed.h0: Discussions with any_procedural_example = 1 have the same view-change rate (delta) as those with any_procedural_example = 0.
decomposed.h1: Discussions with any_procedural_example = 1 have a higher view-change rate than those with any_procedural_example = 0.
decomposed.note: Operational assumption: the "solely abstract" comparison group is operationalized as rows with comments but no comment containing a specific verifiable procedural example; rows where comments are neither abstract rebuttals nor examples (e.g., chatter) fall into 0 too. Association only. OC_comments and conversation may include later replies and view-change announcements; the prompt excludes these as evidence but timing of comments is unknown. The linear model on a binary outcome gives a rate difference.

decomposed.hypothesis: Discussions where the original argument contains specific counter-question markers are associated with a higher probability of view change.

features.name: argument_question_mark_count
features.definition: How many question marks appear in the original argument text?
features.spec: df['argument'].apply(lambda s: s.count('?') if isinstance(s,str) else None). Empty string gives 0; missing/non-string gives null. Counts all '?' characters in current argument text, including quoted text and any edits.  Title and comments are not read.

decomposed.h0: argument_question_mark_count has no association with the probability of view change (delta).
decomposed.h1: Higher argument_question_mark_count is associated with a higher probability of view change.
decomposed.note: "Specific counter-question markers" is not defined in the hypothesis; operationalized as a mechanical literal count of question marks in the argument. This is a proxy: it does not identify rhetorical vs. genuine questions, whether they anticipate counterarguments, or quoted questions. Argument text is current text and may contain edits or outcome announcements (contamination/timing risk); no filtering is applied. OLS on binary delta is a linear probability model; association only, not causal.

decomposed.hypothesis: Discussions where the original poster's argument includes personal anecdotes or first-person experiential narratives are associated with a lower likelihood of view change.

features.name: op_argument_has_personal_anecdote
features.definition: Does the original poster's argument include a personal anecdote or first-person experiential narrative of their own?
features.spec: Read only the `argument` text (OP's own explanation). Return 1 if the OP's own assertions include at least one personal anecdote or first-person experiential narrative (e.g., describing something that happened to them or that they personally did/experienced/witnessed). Return 0 if none. Do not count quotations or stories attributed to other people/sources unless the OP adopts them as their own experience; quotation marks alone do not establish another speaker. Do not count purely abstract opinions, hypotheticals, or general claims. Ignore and do not count OP view-change/delta-award announcements, post-outcome edits/resolution updates, or reports of the outcome as anecdotes. Return null if argument is missing or malformed; empty text gives 0.

decomposed.h0: Discussions whose OP argument includes personal anecdotes (op_argument_has_personal_anecdote=1) have the same likelihood of view change as those without.
decomposed.h1: Discussions whose OP argument includes personal anecdotes (op_argument_has_personal_anecdote=1) have a lower likelihood of view change than those without.
decomposed.note: Association only, tested via OLS (linear probability) on delta. Uses current argument text, which may include edits or outcome announcements (explicitly excluded from the semantic judgment, but timing of edits is unknown). Anecdote presence is binary; intensity not measured.

decomposed.hypothesis: Discussions where counter-arguments explicitly acknowledge the validity of the original post's initial premise before introducing divergence are associated with a higher likelihood of view change.

features.name: comment_acknowledges_premise_then_diverges
features.definition: Does at least one counter-argument comment explicitly acknowledge the validity of the original post's initial premise before introducing divergence from it?
features.spec: Parse OC_comments (JSON list of comments by users other than the OP). Use title and argument only to identify the OP's initial premise/claim. Return 1 if at least one single comment both (a) explicitly acknowledges that the OP's initial premise (or its starting premise/basic point) is valid, correct, reasonable or true, in the commenter's own voice (not merely quoting the OP or a third party without adopting it), and (b) afterwards within that same comment introduces a point of disagreement or divergence (e.g. 'but', 'however', a different consideration). Acknowledgment must come before the divergence in the comment text. Both conditions must co-occur in the same comment; separate comments cannot jointly satisfy it. Return 0 if no comment qualifies, including generic politeness without validating the premise, or agreement with no divergence. Empty comment list gives 0; missing/malformed OC_comments gives null. Ignore any text announcing that the OP changed their view, delta awards, or post-outcome resolution updates; do not treat them as evidence. Generic discussion of delta/platform rules is eligible but is not itself acknowledgment of the premise.

decomposed.h0: There is no association between comment_acknowledges_premise_then_diverges and the likelihood of view change.
decomposed.h1: Discussions with comment_acknowledges_premise_then_diverges = 1 have a higher likelihood of view change than those with 0.
decomposed.note: Operational assumptions: "initial premise" is interpreted from title/argument as currently supplied (may include edits or outcome text; initial text not recoverable). Comments are unordered with no timestamps, so "before" refers only to order within a single comment. Commenter text may contain outcome-related content, which the prompt is told to ignore. Association only, not causal. Outcome modeled by OLS (linear probability).

decomposed.hypothesis: Discussions where counter-arguments employ concrete personal anecdotes are more likely associated with the original poster changing their view than those using abstract reasoning.

features.name: anecdote_comment_share
features.definition: What proportion of the counter-argument comments employ a concrete personal anecdote (the commenter's own specific experience) to argue against the OP?
features.spec: Parse OC_comments (JSON list of comments by users other than the OP). For each comment decide whether the commenter themself relates a concrete, specific personal anecdote/experience (particular events, people or situations they lived through) as part of their counter-argument. Use title/argument only to interpret what the comment is responding to. Do not count hypotheticals, generic examples, or others' stories/quotations unless the commenter adopts them as their own experience. Ignore any text announcing that the OP changed their view, delta awards, or post-outcome resolution updates; these are not evidence. Output = (number of comments meeting the criterion)/(total comments), a float in [0,1]. Empty list -> null; missing/malformed -> null.

features.name: abstract_reasoning_comment_share
features.definition: What proportion of the counter-argument comments rely on abstract reasoning (general principles, logic, or non-personal argument) to argue against the OP?
features.spec: Parse OC_comments (JSON list of comments by users other than the OP). For each comment decide whether its counter-argument is based on abstract reasoning: general principles, logical or conceptual argument, or impersonal generalisations, not grounded in the commenter's own concrete personal experience. Use title/argument only to interpret the target. A comment may count for both this feature and `anecdote_comment_share` if it contains both kinds of content. Ignore OP view-change/delta-award announcements, post-outcome updates, or reports of the outcome. Output = (number of comments meeting the criterion)/(total comments), float in [0,1]. Empty list -> null; missing/malformed -> null.

decomposed.h0: Holding abstract_reasoning_comment_share constant, anecdote_comment_share has no association with the probability that the OP changed their view.
decomposed.h1: Holding abstract_reasoning_comment_share constant, higher anecdote_comment_share is associated with a higher likelihood of the OP changing their view.
decomposed.note: Association only. Both named sides are measured, but the OLS term beta_anecdote is not the exact contrast beta_anecdote minus beta_abstract; it is the anecdote association conditional on abstract share. Shares are not mutually exclusive (a comment may have both; or neither). Comment order/timing unknown; OC_comments may include later content or outcome announcements, which the prompts are told to ignore. Anecdotes are limited to the commenter's own experience; no inspection of rows was annotated.

decomposed.hypothesis: Discussions containing at least three distinct counter-argument comments are associated with a higher probability of the original poster changing their view than those with fewer.

features.name: has_three_plus_comments
features.definition: Does the discussion contain at least three counter-argument comments from other users?
features.spec: Parse OC_comments with json.loads. If missing/malformed or not a list, return null. Let n = number of list entries (empty list -> n=0). Return 1 if n>=3 else 0. Entries are counted as supplied; no deduplication or semantic filtering. Raw list may include outcome-related text; not filtered.

decomposed.h0: Discussions with at least three counter-argument comments (has_three_plus_comments=1) have the same probability of OP view change as those with fewer.
decomposed.h1: Discussions with has_three_plus_comments=1 have a higher probability of OP view change than those with fewer than three.
