features.name: counterarg_cognitive_complexity
features.definition: Across the counter-argument comments, how cognitively complex is the reasoning on average (differentiating multiple perspectives or considerations and integrating them), rated 1-5?
features.spec: Parse OC_comments (JSON list of comments by users other than OP). Use title/argument only to interpret the target. For each comment, rate cognitive complexity of the commenter's own reasoning on 1-5: 1=single undifferentiated assertion, no nuance; 2=simple reasoning with one consideration; 3=acknowledges more than one consideration or perspective or a qualification; 4=differentiates several perspectives/conditions and weighs them; 5=differentiates and integrates multiple perspectives into a coherent higher-level synthesis. Return the mean rating across comments as a single number. Ignore quoted text from others unless the commenter adopts it. Ignore any OP view-change/delta-award announcements, post-outcome updates and reports of the outcome as evidence. Empty list gives null; malformed or missing input gives null.

decomposed.h0: counterarg_cognitive_complexity has no association with the likelihood of delta (coefficient equals 0).
decomposed.h1: Higher counterarg_cognitive_complexity is associated with a higher likelihood of delta (coefficient greater than 0).
decomposed.note: Cognitive complexity is not defined in the hypothesis; the 1-5 rubric (differentiation and integration) and mean aggregation across comments are operational assumptions. Outcome is binary delta, fitted with OLS (linear probability). Association only, not causal. OC_comments order carries no chronology; comments may contain outcome-related text, which the prompt is told to ignore. Current text only, with no timestamps.

decomposed.hypothesis: Discussions where counter-arguments explicitly acknowledge the original poster's underlying valid point before introducing the discrepancy are associated with higher view-change rates than pure refutations.

features.name: any_comment_acknowledges_valid_point_before_discrepancy
features.definition: Does at least one counter-argument comment explicitly acknowledge a valid underlying point of the OP before introducing a discrepancy or disagreement in that same comment?
features.spec: Parse OC_comments (JSON list of other users' comments; order is not chronology). Use title and argument only to interpret what the OP's point is. Return 1 if at least one single comment explicitly acknowledges that the OP has a valid underlying point (in its own voice, not merely quoting the OP) AND then, later in that same comment, introduces a discrepancy, counterpoint or disagreement. Acknowledgment and discrepancy must co-occur in the same comment; separate comments cannot jointly satisfy it. Return 0 if comments exist but none do (including pure refutations, or agreement without any discrepancy). Empty list gives 0; missing or malformed OC_comments gives null. Ignore any OP view-change/delta-award announcements, post-outcome resolution updates or reports of the outcome; do not treat them as acknowledgment evidence. Generic delta-rule discussion is eligible but not itself acknowledgment.

decomposed.h0: any_comment_acknowledges_valid_point_before_discrepancy has no association with delta (view-change) rate.
decomposed.h1: Discussions with any_comment_acknowledges_valid_point_before_discrepancy = 1 have higher view-change rates than those with 0.
decomposed.note: Operational assumption: the "pure refutation" comparison group is rows where no comment satisfies the acknowledge-then-discrepancy pattern (feature = 0), which also includes mixed rows and rows with agreeing or neutral comments. Comment order and timing are unknown; "before" is assessed only within a single comment's text. OC_comments may contain post-outcome content, and the semantic spec excludes outcome announcements. Association only, not causal.

decomposed.hypothesis: Discussions where counter-arguments reference specific, named external programs or locations are associated with higher view-change rates than those using only abstract logical refutation.

features.name: any_named_program_or_place_reference
features.definition: Does at least one counter-argument comment refer to a specific, named external program or location as part of its argument?
features.spec: Parse OC_comments (JSON list of comments by users other than the OP). Return 1 if at least one comment itself refers to a specific, proper-named external program (e.g., a named government/social/educational/software program or initiative) or a specific named location (e.g., a named city, country, institution site) as an example, evidence or illustration in its argument. Generic unnamed categories ('some programs', 'a city') do not count. Names appearing only inside text quoted from someone else count only if the commenter adopts them as support. Ignore any OP view-change/delta-award announcements, post-outcome resolution updates or reports of the outcome; they are not evidence. Return 0 if the list is valid and no comment qualifies, or if the list is empty; null if missing or malformed.

features.name: only_abstract_logical_refutation
features.definition: Do the counter-argument comments rely solely on abstract logical refutation, with no reference to any specific named external program or location?
features.spec: Parse OC_comments (comments by users other than the OP). Return 1 if the list is non-empty, at least one comment makes a counter-argument by abstract reasoning (logical refutation, principles, hypotheticals, conceptual distinctions), and NO comment refers to a specific proper-named external program or named location. Return 0 if any comment references a specific named program or location, or if no comment offers abstract logical refutation (e.g., only other kinds of content). Ignore OP view-change/delta-award announcements, post-outcome updates or reports of the outcome. Null if the list is empty, missing or malformed (no comparison group defined).

decomposed.h0: There is no association between any_named_program_or_place_reference and delta, holding only_abstract_logical_refutation fixed.
decomposed.h1: Discussions with any_named_program_or_place_reference have higher view-change rates than those with only_abstract_logical_refutation.
decomposed.note: Both comparison groups are measured; the coefficient on the named-reference feature is not the direct contrast with the abstract-only group (neither-group cases, e.g., concrete but unnamed examples, remain in the reference category). Comment text is current, unordered, and may contain outcome announcements, which the prompts exclude. Association only; 'named program or location' judged by an LLM with no fixed scale.

decomposed.hypothesis: Discussions where counter-arguments explicitly quote and refute specific phrases from the original post are associated with a higher likelihood of view change.

features.name: any_comment_quotes_and_refutes_op_phrase
features.definition: Does at least one counter-argument comment explicitly quote a specific phrase from the original post and refute it in that same comment?
features.spec: Parse OC_comments (JSON list of comments by other users). Return 1 if at least one single comment both (a) explicitly quotes (verbatim or near-verbatim, e.g. in quotation marks or blockquote) a specific phrase from the OP's title or argument, and (b) disputes, rebuts or refutes that quoted phrase in the same comment. Use title/argument only to verify that the quoted phrase comes from the OP. Quoting without refuting, refuting without quoting, or quote and refutation split across different comments gives 0. Quotes of other sources do not count. Ignore any content that is an OP view-change/delta-award announcement, post-outcome resolution update or report of the outcome; such content is not evidence. Empty list gives 0; missing or malformed OC_comments gives null.

decomposed.h0: any_comment_quotes_and_refutes_op_phrase has no association with delta (coefficient = 0).
decomposed.h1: any_comment_quotes_and_refutes_op_phrase is positively associated with delta (coefficient > 0).
decomposed.note: Operationalized "discussions where counter-arguments quote and refute" as at least one comment doing both. OLS on binary delta (linear probability model); association only. Comment order and timing unknown; OC_comments may contain post-outcome text, which is excluded from the semantic judgment. Quoting judged against current OP text, which may include edits.

decomposed.hypothesis: Discussions where counter-arguments explicitly refute specific examples or anecdotes provided by the original poster are associated with a higher probability of view change compared to arguments addressing the main premise directly.

features.name: refutes_op_example_share
features.definition: What proportion of the counter-argument comments explicitly refute a specific example or anecdote given by the OP?
features.spec: Parse OC_comments (JSON list of other users' comments). Use title and argument only to identify the OP's specific examples/anecdotes (concrete cases, personal experiences) as the target. For each comment, decide whether the commenter's own assertion explicitly refutes, rebuts or discredits a specific OP example or anecdote (not merely the general premise). Quoted text counts only if the commenter adopts it. Ignore any OP view-change/delta-award announcements, post-outcome updates or reports of outcome as evidence. Output = number of such comments / total comments, in [0,1]. Empty list: null. Malformed/missing input: null. Comments are unordered; no chronology implied.

features.name: addresses_main_premise_share
features.definition: What proportion of the counter-argument comments address the OP's main premise directly rather than a specific OP example or anecdote?
features.spec: Parse OC_comments. Use title and argument to identify the OP's main premise (central claim) and any specific examples/anecdotes. For each comment, decide whether its own argument targets the main premise/general claim directly and does not primarily refute a specific OP example or anecdote. Quoted text counts only if adopted by the commenter. Ignore OP view-change/delta-award announcements, post-outcome updates and reports of the outcome. Output = such comments / total comments, in [0,1]. Empty list: null; malformed/missing: null. Comments may be neither type; share of neither is not counted.

decomposed.h0: Holding refutes_op_example_share fixed relative to addresses_main_premise_share, the probability of view change does not differ by refutes_op_example_share (its coefficient is 0).
decomposed.h1: Higher refutes_op_example_share is associated with a higher probability of view change, controlling for addresses_main_premise_share.
decomposed.note: Both comparison sides are measured as shares, but the contrast beta_example - beta_premise is not directly expressible; the tested term is the example-refutation coefficient conditional on premise share. Comments can be neither type, so shares need not sum to 1. Operational assumption: OP examples/anecdotes are identified from current title/argument text, which may include edits or outcome announcements (excluded from semantic judgments, but timing is unknown). OC_comments may include later replies; no timestamps. Association only, via OLS on the binary delta (linear probability).

decomposed.hypothesis: Discussions where the original argument uses hedging or qualifying language are associated with a higher likelihood of view change than those using absolute declarative statements.

features.name: op_argument_hedging_share
features.definition: What proportion of the OP's own assertive sentences in the argument body use hedging or qualifying language (e.g., 'might', 'perhaps', 'in some cases', 'I think', 'generally') rather than absolute declarative phrasing?
features.spec: Read only `argument` (OP's own text). Split into sentences; consider sentences making the OP's own claims/assertions (exclude questions, quoted text attributed to others unless the OP adopts it, and any edit/announcement of view change, delta awards, or outcome/resolution updates). Return count of such sentences containing hedging or qualifying language (epistemic softeners, probability/frequency qualifiers, scope limiters like 'some', 'usually', 'may', 'I think', 'arguably') divided by the number of such assertive sentences. Result in [0,1]. Return null if argument is missing/malformed or has no assertive sentences.

features.name: op_argument_absolute_share
features.definition: What proportion of the OP's own assertive sentences in the argument body are absolute declarative statements without hedging or qualification (e.g., 'always', 'never', 'obviously', flat claims)?
features.spec: Read only `argument` (OP's own text). Consider the OP's own assertive sentences (exclude questions, quotations attributed to others unless adopted, and view-change/delta announcements, outcome reports or post-outcome updates). Return the count of those sentences stated as unqualified absolute declaratives (no hedging or scope qualification) divided by the number of such assertive sentences. Range [0,1]. Null if argument missing/malformed or no assertive sentences.

decomposed.h0: Discussions with higher op_argument_hedging_share have no different likelihood of view change (delta) than those with lower share, holding op_argument_absolute_share constant.
decomposed.h1: Higher op_argument_hedging_share is associated with a higher likelihood of view change, relative to op_argument_absolute_share.
decomposed.note: Both comparison sides are measured, but the two shares are not exactly complementary (some sentences are neither), so the hedging coefficient is not a direct contrast of hedging versus absolute. Argument text is current text and may contain edits or outcome announcements; these are excluded from the semantic measurement, but timing is unknown. Association only, OLS on binary delta (linear probability).

decomposed.hypothesis: Discussions where counter-arguments explicitly quote the original poster's text rather than paraphrasing are associated with a higher probability of view change.

features.name: any_comment_quotes_op
features.definition: Does at least one counter-argument comment explicitly quote the original poster's own text (title or argument) verbatim or near-verbatim?
features.spec: Parse OC_comments (JSON list of other users' comments). Output 1 if at least one comment explicitly reproduces a passage of the OP's text (title or argument) word-for-word or near word-for-word, e.g. in quotation marks or a '>' block quote, and the passage actually matches the OP's title/argument. Quoted text from other sources or other users does not count; quotation marks alone are not enough, the text must match the OP's text. Paraphrase or summary without reproduced wording does not count. Ignore any OP view-change/delta announcements or outcome reports. Output 0 if the list is valid but empty or has no such comment. Null if OC_comments is missing or malformed. Current text only; reply timing unknown.

features.name: any_comment_paraphrases_op_without_quote
features.definition: Does at least one counter-argument comment restate the original poster's position in its own words, without reproducing the OP's wording, as its way of referring to the OP?
features.spec: Parse OC_comments. Output 1 if at least one comment paraphrases or summarises the OP's claims or argument (title/argument) in its own words without verbatim quotation of OP text within that comment. Comments that quote the OP do not count for this feature. Ignore OP view-change/delta announcements or outcome reports. Output 0 if the list is valid but empty or no comment qualifies. Null if OC_comments is missing or malformed.

decomposed.h0: Discussions with any_comment_quotes_op=1 have the same probability of view change as those with 0, holding any_comment_paraphrases_op_without_quote constant.
decomposed.h1: Discussions with any_comment_quotes_op=1 have a higher probability of view change than those with 0, holding any_comment_paraphrases_op_without_quote constant.
decomposed.note: Operationalised at row level as any-comment presence. "Rather than paraphrasing" is approximated by controlling for paraphrase presence; the coefficient is not a strict quote-vs-paraphrase contrast within comments. Comments may both quote and paraphrase. OC_comments may contain later replies and outcome text, timing unknown; delta announcements are excluded from the semantic judgments. Association only, linear probability model.

decomposed.hypothesis: Discussions containing counter-arguments that explicitly validate the original poster's emotional experience prior to logical rebuttal are associated with higher view-change rates.

features.name: any_validates_emotion_before_rebuttal
features.definition: Does at least one counter-argument comment explicitly validate the OP's emotional experience before giving a logical rebuttal in that same comment?
features.spec: Parse OC_comments (JSON list of other users' comments). Use title and argument only to interpret what the OP's emotional experience is. Return 1 if at least one single comment explicitly acknowledges or validates the OP's feelings/emotional experience (e.g., 'I understand why you feel frustrated', 'that sounds painful') in its own words, and this validation appears earlier in the comment than that comment's logical rebuttal/counter-argument to the OP's view. Both elements must occur in the same comment; separate comments cannot combine. Validation of only the argument's logic, generic politeness, or quoted text not adopted by the commenter does not count. Ignore any OP view-change/delta announcements, post-outcome updates, or reports of the outcome as evidence. Return 0 if no comment qualifies, including when the list is valid but empty; null if OC_comments is missing or malformed.

decomposed.h0: any_validates_emotion_before_rebuttal has no association with delta (view-change) rate.
decomposed.h1: Discussions with any_validates_emotion_before_rebuttal = 1 have a higher view-change rate than those with 0.
decomposed.note: Association only. Order within a comment is judged by text position; comment list order/chronology is unknown. OC_comments may contain later replies or outcome-related text, which the prompt excludes as evidence; timing relative to the outcome is unknown. 'Emotional experience' is the OP's, interpreted from title/argument.

decomposed.hypothesis: Discussions containing counter-arguments that use analogies to familiar scenarios are associated with a higher likelihood of the original poster changing their view.

features.name: any_analogy_counterargument
features.definition: Does at least one counter-argument comment use an analogy to a familiar scenario to make its point?
features.spec: Parse OC_comments (JSON list of comments by users other than the OP). Return 1 if at least one comment itself uses an analogy comparing the OP's issue to a different, familiar or everyday scenario (e.g., 'it's like ...', a parallel everyday situation) to support its counter-argument; return 0 if none do. Count only the commenter's own analogies, not analogies merely quoted from others and rebutted without adoption. Ignore any OP view-change/delta-award announcements, thanks for changed view, or reports of the outcome as evidence. Literal examples of the topic itself are not analogies. Empty list gives 0; missing or malformed input gives null.

decomposed.h0: any_analogy_counterargument has no association with the likelihood of delta (OP changing view).
decomposed.h1: Discussions with any_analogy_counterargument=1 have a higher likelihood of the OP changing their view.
decomposed.note: Operational assumption: 'discussions containing' means at least one available counter-argument comment has an analogy. 'Familiar scenario' is judged by the annotator. OC_comments may include later replies or outcome announcements and reply timing is unknown; semantic exclusion applied. Association only, not causal. OLS on binary outcome is a linear probability model.

decomposed.hypothesis: Discussions where the title explicitly contains an absolute universal quantifier like 'all' or 'never' are associated with lower view change than those using variable or probabilistic terms.

features.name: title_has_universal_quantifier
features.definition: Does the title explicitly contain an absolute universal quantifier such as 'all' or 'never'?
features.spec: If title is missing/non-string return null. Lowercase the title; return 1 if re.search(r"\b(all|every|everyone|everybody|everything|always|never|no one|nobody|none|nothing|any and all|entirely|completely|absolutely)\b", t) else 0. Empty string gives 0. Literal word-list match on the current title; the title may contain outcome text in principle (not filtered).

features.name: title_has_variable_probabilistic_term
features.definition: Does the title contain a variable or probabilistic term such as 'some', 'often' or 'usually'?
features.spec: If title is missing/non-string return null. Lowercase the title; return 1 if re.search(r"\b(some|sometimes|often|usually|generally|typically|mostly|most|many|few|several|occasionally|frequently|rarely|seldom|may|might|could|can|probably|likely|unlikely|perhaps|possibly|tend|tends|tend to|majority|minority)\b", t) else 0. Empty string gives 0. Literal word-list match.

features.name: title_universal_vs_probabilistic
features.definition: Among titles containing exactly one of the two term types, is the term type absolute universal (1) rather than variable/probabilistic (0)?
features.spec: Using df['title_has_universal_quantifier'] (u) and df['title_has_variable_probabilistic_term'] (p): return 1 if u==1 and p==0; 0 if u==0 and p==1; null (NaN) if both are 1, both are 0, or either is null. Rows with neither or both term types are excluded from the comparison.

decomposed.h0: Among discussions whose titles contain exactly one term type, title_universal_vs_probabilistic has no association with delta (coefficient = 0).
decomposed.h1: Discussions with universal-quantifier titles (title_universal_vs_probabilistic = 1) have lower view-change rates than those with variable/probabilistic-term titles (coefficient < 0).
decomposed.note: Operational assumptions: the hypothesis gives only examples ('all', 'never'; 'variable or probabilistic terms'), so fixed word lists are my assumption and may omit or over-include (e.g., 'can', 'any', 'most' are ambiguous without context; no semantic check of whether the quantifier governs the claim). Comparison requires both named groups, so rows with neither or both term types are dropped (missing values removed by OLS), leaving a reduced sample. Title is current supplied text; possible outcome contamination is not filtered. Association only, not causal.

decomposed.hypothesis: Discussions containing counter-arguments that explicitly reference specific, concrete examples or real-world instances in the provided comments are associated with a higher probability of view change.

features.name: any_comment_cites_concrete_example
features.definition: Does at least one counter-argument comment explicitly reference a specific, concrete example or real-world instance?
features.spec: Parse OC_comments (JSON list of other users' comments). Return 1 if at least one comment itself explicitly references a specific, concrete example or real-world instance (named person, event, case, place, study, product, or a particular described real situation) to support its counter-argument; generic abstractions or hypotheticals with no specific instance do not count. Use title/argument only to interpret the comment's target. Ignore text announcing that the OP changed their view, delta awards, or post-outcome resolution updates; do not treat them as evidence. Generic delta-rule discussion is eligible but is not itself an example. Return 0 if no comment qualifies, including an empty list; null if OC_comments is missing or malformed.

decomposed.h0: any_comment_cites_concrete_example has no association with the probability of view change (delta).
decomposed.h1: Discussions with any_comment_cites_concrete_example = 1 have a higher probability of view change than those with 0.
decomposed.note: Operationalized as presence of at least one such comment ("containing"); no threshold on count was supplied. Linear probability model via OLS. Comments are unordered with unknown timing; comment text may contain outcome announcements, which the prompt is told to ignore. Association only, not causal.

decomposed.hypothesis: Discussions where counter-arguments contain specific empirical evidence are more likely to be associated with the original poster changing their view than those containing only logical refutations.

features.name: any_counter_specific_empirical_evidence
features.definition: Does at least one counter-argument comment by another user offer specific empirical evidence (e.g., concrete data, statistics, studies, documented cases or verifiable facts) against the OP's view?
features.spec: Parse OC_comments (JSON list of other users' comments; title/argument give context for the OP's view). Return 1 if at least one comment itself asserts or cites specific empirical evidence (named study, statistic, data, documented real-world case, verifiable factual finding) bearing against the OP's view; an external source cited as support counts, without being the commenter's own experience. Generic claims, pure reasoning, opinions or vague appeals to 'facts' do not count. Ignore any OP view-change/delta-award announcements, post-outcome resolution updates and reports of the outcome as evidence. Return 0 if none qualify (including a valid empty list); null if OC_comments is missing or malformed. List order is not chronology.

features.name: counter_only_logical_refutation
features.definition: Do the counter-argument comments contain logical refutations of the OP's view but no specific empirical evidence in any comment?
features.spec: Parse OC_comments (title/argument give context for the OP's view). Return 1 if at least one comment offers a logical refutation (reasoning, inconsistency, counter-example by argument, conceptual or definitional rebuttal) of the OP's view AND no comment contains specific empirical evidence (named study, statistic, data, documented real-world case, verifiable factual finding). Return 0 if any comment contains specific empirical evidence, or if no comment contains a logical refutation (e.g., empty list). Ignore OP view-change/delta-award announcements, post-outcome updates and reports of the outcome as evidence. Null if OC_comments is missing or malformed.

decomposed.h0: Holding counter_only_logical_refutation fixed, any_counter_specific_empirical_evidence is not associated with the probability of the OP changing their view.
decomposed.h1: Discussions with any_counter_specific_empirical_evidence=1 have higher probability of OP view change than those with only logical refutations (counter_only_logical_refutation=1).
decomposed.note: The claimed contrast is empirical-evidence vs logical-only. In this model the reference group is neither (no refutation/evidence), so beta of the empirical term is empirical vs neither, not empirical minus logical-only; the contrast beta_emp - beta_logic is not directly expressible as a single term. Associations only, not causal. Text is current supplied text; comments lack timestamps, and OC_comments/conversation may contain outcome announcements, which the prompts exclude as evidence. The 'only logical' group is operationalized as logical refutation with no empirical evidence in any comment; mixed discussions count as empirical.

decomposed.hypothesis: Discussions where counter-arguments explicitly acknowledge the validity of a specific component of the original argument before presenting a counter-example are associated with higher view change rates.

features.name: ack_then_counterexample
features.definition: Does at least one counter-argument comment explicitly acknowledge the validity of a specific component of the OP's argument and then, in that same comment, present a counter-example?
features.spec: Parse OC_comments (JSON list of comments by users other than OP). Use title and argument only to interpret what the OP's components are. Return 1 if at least one single comment, in its own assertions (not merely quoted text from others), both (a) explicitly acknowledges that a specific identifiable component (a claim, premise or point) of the OP's argument is valid/correct/fair, and (b) AFTER that acknowledgment in the same comment presents a counter-example (a concrete case or instance that challenges the OP's view). Both must occur in the same comment; separate comments cannot jointly satisfy it. Generic politeness, vague agreement or acknowledgment of the OP's effort without naming a component does not count. Return 0 if the list is valid and no comment qualifies, including an empty list. Return null if OC_comments is missing or malformed. Ignore any OP view-change/delta-award announcements, post-outcome resolution updates or reports of the outcome as evidence; do not treat them as acknowledgment or counter-example.

decomposed.h0: ack_then_counterexample has no association with the probability of view change (delta).
decomposed.h1: Discussions with ack_then_counterexample = 1 have higher view-change rates than those with 0.
decomposed.note: Linear probability model via OLS on delta; association only. OC_comments are unordered with no timestamps, so "before" is judged only by order within a single comment's text. Comments may contain contamination from view-change announcements or later replies; the prompt excludes these as evidence. Current text may include edits. Acknowledgment of a 'specific component' is a judgment by the annotator.

decomposed.hypothesis: Discussions where counter-arguments utilize second-person direct address are associated with higher original poster view-change rates than arguments relying on third-person analysis.

features.name: share_second_person_address_comments
features.definition: What proportion of counter-argument comments use second-person direct address to the OP (e.g., addressing the OP as 'you' about their view or reasoning)?
features.spec: Parse OC_comments (JSON list of comments by users other than the OP). For each comment decide whether the comment's own wording directly addresses the OP in the second person (e.g., 'you say', 'your argument', 'you might consider'), using title and argument only to interpret the target. Generic 'you' meaning people in general, and 'you' inside quotations of other speakers not adopted by the commenter, do not count. Ignore any content that announces an OP view change/delta award, post-outcome updates or reports of the outcome; such content is not evidence. Output the number of qualifying comments divided by the number of comments (0 to 1). Empty list: null. Malformed/missing: null. Comment order carries no meaning.

features.name: share_third_person_analysis_comments
features.definition: What proportion of counter-argument comments rely on third-person analysis of the issue (discussing the topic, people or the OP's position impersonally, without addressing the OP directly)?
features.spec: Parse OC_comments (JSON list of comments by users other than the OP). For each comment decide whether its argument is mainly third-person/impersonal analysis (about the topic, groups, evidence, or 'the view'/'the OP' in third person) and does NOT rely on second-person direct address to the OP; use title and argument only to interpret the target. Comments that mainly address the OP as 'you/your' do not count; quotations of others not adopted do not count as the commenter's style. Ignore content announcing OP view change/delta awards, post-outcome updates or reports of the outcome. Output qualifying comments divided by total comments (0 to 1). Empty list: null. Malformed/missing: null. Comment order carries no meaning.

decomposed.h0: Controlling for share_third_person_analysis_comments, share_second_person_address_comments is not associated with delta (view-change) likelihood.
decomposed.h1: Controlling for share_third_person_analysis_comments, higher share_second_person_address_comments is associated with higher delta (view-change) likelihood.
decomposed.note: Operationalised at discussion level as the share of comments in each style; styles can overlap or neither apply, so both shares are included. The coefficient on the second-person share is not a direct second-vs-third contrast (beta_A - beta_B), which this contract cannot express. Comments are unordered and may include later replies; conversation was not used. Comment text may contain delta/view-change announcements (contamination risk); the prompts exclude them. Association only, not causal.

decomposed.hypothesis: Original posts with direct personal anecdotes in the argument are associated with a lower probability of the original poster changing their view.

features.name: argument_has_direct_personal_anecdote
features.definition: Does the OP's argument text contain a direct personal anecdote, i.e. the OP recounting their own firsthand experience or an event in their own life?
features.spec: Read only the `argument` text (OP's own words). Return 1 if the OP, in their own assertions, recounts at least one direct personal anecdote: a specific firsthand experience or event from their own life (e.g. 'when I worked at X, I saw...', 'my brother and I once...'). Return 0 if there is none: only abstract claims, general reasoning, hypotheticals, statistics, or experiences of others/external sources quoted but not adopted as the OP's own experience. Quotation marks alone do not establish another speaker; judge by who the experience belongs to. Do not count OP view-change/delta-award announcements, edits reporting the outcome, or post-outcome resolution updates as anecdotes. Do not use the title or comments. Return null if argument is missing or malformed; an empty argument gives 0.

decomposed.h0: Argument_has_direct_personal_anecdote has no association with the probability of OP changing their view (delta).
decomposed.h1: Posts with argument_has_direct_personal_anecdote = 1 have a lower probability of delta = 1 than posts without.
decomposed.note: Association only, using a linear probability OLS. Uses current argument text, which may include edits or outcome announcements; the prompt excludes these, but the timing of the text relative to the outcome is unknown. 'Direct personal anecdote' is interpreted as the OP's own firsthand story; the threshold is judged by the annotator.

decomposed.hypothesis: Discussions where the original argument addresses the reader using second-person direct address are associated with a higher likelihood of view change than those using impersonal phrasing.

decomposed.hypothesis: Discussions where counter-arguments employ specific, concrete illustrative examples are associated with a higher probability of the original poster changing their view.

features.name: share_oc_with_concrete_examples

decomposed.hypothesis: Posts with more counter-arguments containing specific real-world examples are more likely to be associated with the original poster changing their view.

features.name: count_oc_comments_with_real_world_examples

features.definition: What proportion of counter-argument comments explicitly acknowledge the OP's view as valid or partly valid before introducing a narrower, specific caveat?

Use title and argument only to interpret the comment's target. Acknowledgement of something other than the OP's view, or acknowledgement without a following specific caveat, does not count. features.spec: Parse OC_comments (JSON list of comments by other users). For each comment decide whether it opens by directly and broadly contradicting or rejecting the OP's overall view (a general, sweeping disagreement rather than a narrow, specific caveat) without first explicitly acknowledging any validity in the OP's view. Use title and argument only to interpret the target. Comments that acknowledge validity first, or only raise narrow caveats, or are non-contradicting, do not count. Ignore quoted text unless adopted by the commenter. Exclude any OP view-change/delta-award announcements, post-outcome updates and reports of the outcome as evidence. OP concessions would have to be read from conversation or later OP text, which can include view-change/delta announcements and post-outcome updates, so the measure would reveal or closely proxy the outcome. No cleaned concession proxy is substituted, and the OP-concession measurement is not defined as a feature. Only the predictor side (presence of a well-reasoned counterargument) is measured, and "engaging with" is operationalized as such a comment being present, since it is unknown whether the OP engaged. Because the OLS outcome is delta, term=null. Reply timing and links are unknown. Associations only, not causal.

decomposed.hypothesis: Discussions where counter-arguments contain specific numerical data or statistics are associated with a higher likelihood of original-poster view change than those relying on general assertions.

features.name: share_comments_with_numerical_data
features.definition: What proportion of the counter-argument comments contain specific numerical data or statistics (as opposed to only general assertions)?
features.spec: Parse OC_comments (JSON list of comments by users other than the OP). For each comment decide whether the commenter's own text presents specific numerical data or statistics as support (e.g., concrete figures, percentages, rates, counts, study results with numbers, dated quantitative facts), including numbers attributed to a cited external source. Do not count vague quantifiers ('many', 'most'), numbers that are not evidential data (list numbering, 'two reasons', times/dates used only as labels, usernames), or purely hypothetical made-up numbers. Exclude any text that announces an OP view change/delta award or reports the discussion outcome; delta-rule discussion is eligible but is not itself numerical evidence. Return number of comments meeting this divided by total number of comments, a value in [0,1]. Empty list gives null; malformed input gives null.

decomposed.h0: share_comments_with_numerical_data has no association with the likelihood of OP view change (delta).
decomposed.h1: Higher share_comments_with_numerical_data is associated with a higher likelihood of OP view change (delta).
decomposed.note: Operationalization: the contrast 'specific numerical data vs general assertions' is measured as the share of comments with numerical data; the remainder are treated as not using such data (general assertions is not separately measured). Comment order, timing and per-comment outcomes are unavailable. OC_comments may contain post-outcome text; semantic exclusion applied in the prompt. Association only, not causal.
